references.title: The Shade Stitcher
references.silhouette: Tall human, narrow apron, triangular bundle of shade battens rising over one shoulder.
references.motivation: Paid to keep the market's shade intact; another torn panel costs her the afternoon's earnings.
references.quirk: Holds spare pegs between her lips and tests every knot with a hard tug.
references.sceneRole: Her routine lowering and raising of a cloth panel gives Harper a visible escape opportunity to plan for.
references.designProposal: Adult human woman about fifty, tall and sinewy, weathered angular face, short graying hair wrapped back with a plain cloth band. Narrow dusty sage work apron over faded off-white sun layers, narrow loose trousers and worn closed work shoes. Triangular bundle of salvaged shade battens secured over one shoulder, one rolled teal cloth panel at hip, small peg pouch. Two spare blunt pegs held casually between lips; one hand testing a rope knot. No glamour or cute expression.
references.qaNotes: One mature woman, full head and shoes visible, clear knot-testing pose, two pegs held at lips, triangular battens and teal cloth roll legible. Neutral background and painted/ink treatment match. Rope extends off upper edge as a working line; person and key silhouette fully framed. No text or extra characters.

references.title: The Scrap Appraiser
references.silhouette: Small older human, tiered pockets, one oversized folding magnifier.
references.motivation: Buys useful salvage cheaply and fears paying for a worthless part.
references.quirk: Weighs a piece in one palm before ever looking at its seller.
references.sceneRole: Takes an interest in what Taffy is carrying; the boy has to conceal the newly stolen device while appearing ordinary.
references.designProposal: Older short human man, slightly stooped, sharp skeptical eyes and a deeply lived-in face, bald crown and sparse coarse gray hair. Layered rust-gray pocket tabard with graduated rows of worn flat pockets over breathable cream shirt; cropped loose trousers and patched soft work shoes. One oversized hinged folding magnifier, clearly handheld, and a palm-sized generic scrap fitting resting in other palm. Leaning slightly to weigh rather than smiling at viewer. No resemblance to Taffy or the gray alien boss.
references.qaNotes: One older skeptical short man, stooped posture, balding crown, prominent folding magnifier and palm-held pipe fitting, layered tiers of worn pockets. Complete head/hands/shoes framed. Strong distinct silhouette; some dense pocket dressing and wear, suitable first design. No text or extra characters.

references.title: The Quiet Stallholder
references.silhouette: Long-fingered offworld human behind a shallow stall with folding wooden wings.
references.motivation: Needs enough sales to pay tomorrow's rent; dislikes the water broker's cut.
references.quirk: Keeps straightening a single item customers never buy.
references.sceneRole: Notices the children arrive together, then separately; can choose to continue a sale rather than inform the broker. A small decision with moral weight.
references.designProposal: Mature offworld human woman, taller long-fingered proportions, quiet lined face with broad high cheekbones and dark attentive eyes, warm muted olive-brown skin. Simple sun-faded clay-pink crossed shoulder garment over a plain charcoal skirted work layer and ordinary worn footwear; muted woven sleeve cuffs, not the boy's plum costume or repeated cheek marks. Small shallow wooden trading stand with folding side wings, one partly folded, supported on visible spindly legs so the person's lower legs and feet remain visible. A few ceramic clasps and repair fittings arranged sparsely; one hand straightens a single unsold clasp while gaze watches off-frame. One coherent single-character illustration, no full market backdrop.
references.qaNotes: Mature attentive woman with quiet off-frame gaze; one hand straightening ordinary clasp, clear folding trading stand with right wing folded, feet and full head visible. Long-fingered offworld quality remains subtle/humanlike. Garment is clay-pink crossed shoulder wrap with restrained cuffs, shares some wrap construction with boy but distinct adult skirted silhouette. Table stock uses generic ring/clasp fittings without stolen key red inset. No text, extra people or scene backdrop.

references.title: Doorpost
references.silhouette: Broad wedge-shaped humanoid, heavy work coat, one shoulder padded for moving crates.
references.motivation: Paid to keep people away from the boss and treats personal space as a strict boundary.
references.quirk: Turns his whole body instead of just his head.
references.sceneRole: His turns open and close the line of sight to Taffy. He can become the visible pursuer Harper draws into the public passage.
references.designProposal: Large adult male humanoid with broad wedge-shaped upper body, thick short neck and blunt compact head, naturally nonhuman smooth matte desaturated gray-olive biological skin. Small patient eyes, broad flat ear lobes set close to head, rounded blunt nose structure, no forehead ridges and no beast/ape caricature. Heavy but breathable dusty charcoal work coat with one large asymmetric faded blue-gray shoulder pad for carrying crates, unpatterned pale undershirt, broad loose plain trousers and thick repaired work boots. Hands empty; sideways braced stance and whole-body turn suggest he blocks access. Strong imposing silhouette, not plated sci-fi armor, not military tactical webbing.
references.qaNotes: One imposing broad wedge-shaped adult humanoid, empty hands, thick repaired work boots, charcoal coat and one large blue-gray shoulder pad clear, full figure framed. Head/skin are more pebbled and heavy-browed than the requested smooth gray-olive biology, leaning toward broker-family/ape-like geometry. This is an unapproved species design caveat for review, not a locked identity. No weapon, text, extra character or panel.

references.title: Fast Coat
references.silhouette: Long-legged humanoid in a sleeveless coat with two blunt hanging tails.
references.motivation: A junior enforcer hoping that a conspicuous success will earn a better position.
references.quirk: Signals bystanders out of his way as if he already commands them.
references.sceneRole: A fast, committed pursuer makes Harper's decoy route dangerous; she needs concealment and a planned turn to lose him.
references.designProposal: Adult male humanoid in his late twenties, long legs and narrow torso, long angular face, short swept-back dark hair, matte warm gray-taupe skin with subtly unfamiliar wide-set ears, no pointed ears or forehead wrinkles. Sleeveless dusty faded indigo-gray coat with TWO blunt rectangular hanging tails over sand long-sleeved light shirt, close-wrapped lower trouser legs and scuffed flexible boots. One simple repurposed throat fastener, empty hands; a brisk half-step and outward palm clearing the route. Ambitious alert expression, no big grin, no weapon. Silhouette very different from the broad B1 guard.
references.qaNotes: Adult long-legged humanoid, long sleeveless twin-tail coat and outward clearing palm readable; full head, hands and boots visible. Strong angular face, subtle offworld ears. No text, extra figures or weapons. Narrow portrait matches set direction. First visual proposal.

references.title: Valve Hand
references.silhouette: Squat humanoid, oversized padded gloves, short apron marked by mineral deposits.
references.motivation: Maintains the broker's pumps; a damaged valve is his problem even when the boss causes it.
references.quirk: Moves other people's cups off machinery without asking.
references.sceneRole: Can interrupt the jewel exchange to reach a control beside the chair, briefly threatening Taffy's cover without having noticed him.
references.designProposal: Adult compact squat humanoid with barrel torso, short bowed powerful legs, smooth muted copper-clay biological skin and low broad rounded head, small steady eyes. Oversized worn PADDED fabric/leather work gloves, short faded slate apron encrusted with pale mineral deposits over pale tan practical garments, stout repaired work shoes. One glove gently moves a plain metal cup away from a small waist-high salvaged valve block prop, the other checks its handle. The block is a compact work prop, not an environment. Gruff absorbed maintenance worker, no monster exaggeration, no modern machinery brand.
references.qaNotes: Clear squat copper-clay adult humanoid, broad rounded head, oversized padded gloves and mineral-marked slate apron. Cup-moving action and valve readable. Full boots/head/hands present, no text or extra people. Valve prop is somewhat larger than a small block but still a local occupational prop; equipment more elaborate than sparse sketch. Valid first design.

references.title: The Pipe Fitter
references.silhouette: Human with one long protective glove, a shoulder roll of tools and a low work stool.
references.motivation: Must finish a pressure adjustment before the supply cycle changes.
references.quirk: Answers everything with their eyes still on the pressure needle.
references.sceneRole: A valve release masks a few footsteps, while the fitter's work position closes one route. The children must read and time that routine.
references.designProposal: Adult human woman around forty, medium height, wiry compact practical build, sun-browned freckled weathered face, short dark hair tied close at nape. One distinctly LONG protective glove above elbow on one arm and a shorter bare-sleeved opposite arm. Faded ochre-gray utility shirt over plain loose blue-gray trousers, rugged low boots, a shoulder tool roll with a closed flap, low battered folding stool beside her. She stands looking down at a handheld analog pressure gauge, quietly occupied, free arm ready to reach a valve. Different silhouette and equipment from the squat gloved B6; no matching twin outfits.
references.qaNotes: Adult human pipe fitter with asymmetrical long protective gauntlet, readable analog pressure gauge, work bag and low folding stool. Full head/soles/hands framed, plain background, no other figures/text. Face reads somewhat younger than around forty and equipment is a flap satchel plus belt tools rather than a simple rolled bundle; not a blocking issue for first study. Distinct from squat B6.

references.title: The Pressure Warden
references.silhouette: Broad human in a stiff sun cape, carrying a flat inspection board.
references.motivation: Responsible for keeping the public out of working water infrastructure.
references.quirk: Checks a latch twice, even after seeing it catch.
references.sceneRole: Closes the obvious maintenance gate on schedule, forcing a choice of path. Needs an early glimpse of the routine so the obstacle feels earned.
references.designProposal: Adult broad human man late fifties, deliberate grounded posture, full weathered face, sparse graying beard kept short, tired vigilant eyes. Stiff short sun cape in dusty stone/olive canvas creates a clear trapezoidal silhouette; plain loose underlayers and boots, no armor or military uniform. Holds a FLAT rectangular inspection board under one arm; the other hand tests a simple detached latch fixture at waist height on a narrow stand. Matter-of-fact responsible expression, as if checking twice. No writing on board, no weapon or dangling keys that might be mistaken for the stolen key.
references.qaNotes: Broad mature human with graying beard, stiff sun cape, flat unlettered inspection board and hand testing detached latch post. Stern watchful expression and trapezoid cape silhouette clear. Full head, hands, feet visible; no extra people/text/weapons. Props do not hide body. Valid first study.

references.title: The Scrap Sweeper
references.silhouette: Wiry humanoid towing a low bundle of metal with a long magnetic collecting pole.
references.motivation: Paid by recovered weight; hates useful fragments being trampled into the drain.
references.quirk: Taps each piece against the pole and listens before adding it.
references.sceneRole: The pole sweeps across Taffy's path; a metal click from the stolen device could expose him. Creates a small precise obstacle rather than another chase.
references.designProposal: Adult wiry humanoid of ambiguous gender, long bony limbs and long natural fingers, narrow head with smooth matte muted dun-gray skin, short coarse dark crop, humanlike rounded ears. Faded mismatched sleeved work layers, loose narrow trousers, low wrapped work shoes. Long magnetic collecting pole with an obvious dull metal collecting end, small metal fragments and one low bundled drag-sled of recovered fittings tied with cord; nothing weaponlike or sharp pointing at viewer. Holds pole across floor at a shallow angle and raises one tiny scrap to listen when tapped. Different clothing and face from appraiser A3, no cybernetic implants.
qaNotes: Single wiry adult full-body figure with magnetic pole, listening gesture and low scrap sled.
Head, hands, shoes and pole collecting head fully framed; no text or extra characters.
Figure reads mostly human and the scarf/vest retains some cover costume influence; slightly less alien than proposed, usable first reference.

references.title: The Pass Clerk
references.silhouette: Round-helmeted humanoid at a small window, flat permit boards stacked like roof tiles.
references.motivation: Wants an impeccable handover so nobody can blame them for an access error.
references.quirk: Aligns every battered permit edge before putting it down.
references.sceneRole: Adds a human inspection after the key opens the electronic boundary. A raised pen or held stare creates uncertainty without demanding another stolen object.
references.designProposal: Adult round-helmeted nonhuman humanoid clerk, compact slightly pear-shaped body, long calm face with gently downturned wide mouth and muted ashy mauve-gray biological skin, small dark eyes, no cute giant eyes. Low smooth round battered civilian protective helmet leaving whole face visible. Faded cream bureaucratic work smock with plain dusty petrol-blue side panel, practical trousers, modest closed shoes. Small narrow permit desk/window-frame prop beside them, OPEN below so feet visible; stack of flat battered permit boards held and aligned carefully, simple stylus in hand. No writing, no holographic floating UI, no military helmet/armor.
qaNotes: One adult alien clerk with round civilian helmet, permit boards and stylus; frame/desk open below so both shoes visible.
Asymmetric cream/petrol-blue work smock, small calm eyes and deliberate administrative pose read clearly.
Small ordinary U-shaped belt ring present; not the asymmetric stolen key. No writing or duplicate characters.

references.title: The Relay Electrician
references.silhouette: Wiry older human, short utility cape, loops of spare cable over one arm.
references.motivation: Trying to get a failing public display back into service and get paid.
references.quirk: Tests it with the same two-finger tap after every repair.
references.sceneRole: Can bring the screen back at exactly the wrong moment for the children: the successful repair reveals their wanted broadcast. Establish the repair before the reveal.
references.designProposal: Older wiry human woman around sixty-five, deep warm brown skin, closely cut silver hair, long angular face with strong cheekbones and focused tired eyes. Short faded smoky blue utility cape over rolled-sleeve pale work shirt and plain sun-faded brown trousers, scuffed work shoes. Loops of salvaged cable over one forearm and a small repaired hand tester with two broad contacts in other hand; index and middle finger poised for habitual test tap on a compact detached display module at hip height. Cables short enough to manage, no live sparking spectacle, no magic staff, no decorative matching costume.
qaNotes: One older human woman with short silver curls, angular weathered face and short utility cape.
Cable loops, repaired display module and two-contact tester clearly express electrical work; full body/feet framed.
Looks mature but could read somewhat younger than the proposed sixty-five; minor first-reference variation. No writing or extra people.

references.title: The Port Messenger
references.silhouette: Slender offworld humanoid, long calves, one upright rigid delivery tube.
references.motivation: Needs to reach cargo dispatch before its next transfer departs.
references.quirk: Always chooses their next doorway before finishing the current one.
references.sceneRole: Their purposeful exit toward the cargo ramp plants the onward route to the port. When the alert appears, a stopped step and turned head raise the stakes.
references.designProposal: Adult slender offworld humanoid woman around thirty, unusually long calves and narrow frame, long oval face and quiet alert side glance, smooth muted pale sand-gray skin with subtle warm mottling, close dark hair. Plain layered travel shirt with asymmetrical dusty blue-gray outer tabard, cropped charcoal trousers that reveal long shins above flat reinforced walking shoes. ONE upright rigid dented delivery tube held close to body by a simple shoulder loop, broad capped ends, no lettering. Half-turned poised stance already choosing next doorway, economical and brisk rather than heroic. No duplicate of the boy's sack, belt, marks or outfit.
qaNotes: One slender adult offworld woman with long exposed calves, pale mottled skin, dark tied-back hair and an upright capped delivery tube.
Brisk turning glance and wrapped tabard read as travel/messenger; complete head, hands and footwear framed.
Reads relatively young and fairly attractive compared with no-model-pose guidance, but not a child or glamour pose; acceptable initial adult reference. No text or extra figures.
